beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The useful promise is exchange capacity inside a network with shared rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Acceptance, credit limits, and responsibility for default still need institutional answers.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book places such experiments beside local currencies and other monetary alternatives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Their differences matter more than collecting everything beneath a single complementary currency label.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading the cases shows why an appealing design can still struggle to survive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The historical journey makes plurality harder to dismiss as a recent digital novelty.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Commodity, credit, state authority, and social relationships offer different explanations of monetary life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book brings monetary thinkers into conversation with the institutions they hoped to change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: These perspectives disagree about which problem money should solve and whose freedom matters.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They provide alternative questions, rather than a parade leading inevitably toward cryptocurrency.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That prepares the reader to see digital systems as choices with inherited tensions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The past becomes a resource for judgment, not evidence that every experiment deserves revival.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Digital scarcity and programmable transfers change what a monetary system can automate.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They do not remove every relationship on which a user must rely.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows trust into software, governance, custody, interfaces, and connections with external facts.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A rule enforced automatically still raises questions about who wrote and can change it.
